decisions.mark: names MBEDTLS_THREADING_C and MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD as the gating macros
decisions.detail: QUOTE: Every mutex in the tree sits behind `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C`, which ships off. ... The index was built with `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` and `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` forced on by flag | WHY: The answer names both MBEDTLS_THREADING_C as the gate on locks and MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD, which it describes only as a flag the index was built with, so naming it as a gating macro is thin but present.

decisions.mark: states that the shipped mbedtls_config.h leaves BOTH threading macros undefined, so a default build defines neither
decisions.detail: QUOTE: Default build (`MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` off, `mbedtls_config.h:3787`) … `MBEDTLS_THREADING_ALT` is also off by default (`mbedtls_config.h:2185`) | WHY: The answer says `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` and `MBEDTLS_THREADING_ALT` are off by default. It never says `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` is off, and the caveat says the default claim was not confirmed from the shipped config. The item probably means the C/PTHREAD pair, and I can't tell that from the answer, so this resolves to MISS.

decisions.mark: concludes that a default build of mbedtls creates no threads at all, and that the pthread example compiles to a stub main under that condition
decisions.detail: QUOTE: Every mutex in the tree sits behind `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C`, which ships off. ... That file is gated on `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` (lines 24–492), so it is not built by default. | WHY: The answer lists threads that exist (including signal handlers and timer procs) and never concludes that a default build creates no threads at all. It also never says the pthread example compiles to a stub main, only that it is "not built by default".

decisions.mark: states BOTH halves of the contrast: that nothing in library/ creates a thread, AND that library/ nonetheless supplies the mutex abstraction used by threaded callers
decisions.detail: QUOTE: NONE | WHY: The answer says threads exist only outside `library/` and that `library/threading.c` holds the mutex abstraction. It never states the contrast directly: that nothing in `library/` creates a thread, yet `library/` supplies the mutex abstraction for threaded callers.
